title: Written in the Stars: Armin Strom Enters a Universe of Meteorite-Dial Watches
content:
Novelties

From cosmic origins to mechanical brilliance, Armin Strom’s new Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite puts the universe on display, alongside five other watches celebrating this extraordinary material.

There is something extraordinary about wearing a piece of the universe on your wrist. Meteorite dials feature naturally occurring patterns formed long before Earth existed, making every slice unique.

Beyond their appearance, they bring a touch of nature to objects defined by precision and engineering.

Armin Strom is one brand that explores this contrast. Known for its mechanical transparency and expertise in resonance, the independent manufacture brings these worlds together in its latest creation: the Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite.

Alongside this new release, discover five more watches putting meteorite dials in the spotlight.

The Armin Strom Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite

Armin Strom has never done things by halves, particularly when it comes to resonance. Its latest creation combines one of the brand’s defining mechanical signatures with a material literally out of this world: natural meteorite.

Limited to 15 pieces, the Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite offers a striking interpretation of the brand’s dual-time concept, pairing two meteorite displays with its sophisticated in-house resonance movement. Beyond its distinctive dial, considerable mechanical complexity lies beneath the surface.

A Natural Choice

Both dials are crafted from natural meteorite, giving each watch a unique pattern. Their grey tones create an almost lunar landscape, complemented by black azurage chapter rings, polished rose-gold-coloured indexes and faceted hands. Polished and blackened steel day/night discs add further contrast.

The displays sit within a 39mm stainless-steel case measuring just 9.05mm thick, paired with a matte grey alligator strap.

The result balances the meteorite’s natural irregularity with the precision and refined finishing expected of the Biel/Bienne manufacture.

The Science of Staying in Sync

The real story lies inside. The manually wound ARF22 calibre is entirely designed, developed and produced in-house by Armin Strom. It features two independent regulating systems, each displaying its own hours, minutes and day/night indications.

The systems are connected by the patented Resonance Clutch, allowing the balance wheels to interact and synchronise through resonance. Comprising 231 components and 40 jewels, the movement beats at 3.5 Hz (25,200 vibrations per hour) and offers a 42-hour power reserve, visible through the sapphire caseback.

A fitting combination of extraterrestrial material and mechanical innovation, the watch is limited to 15 pieces worldwide and priced at CHF 105,000.

Piaget Andy Warhol Clou de Paris

Piaget takes a different approach with the Andy Warhol watch, combining its distinctive Clou de Paris case with a blue meteorite dial. Here, the emphasis is on shape, texture and personality rather than mechanical theatre.

The richly textured case measures 45 x 43mm, with generous cushion-like proportions. Its blue meteorite dial introduces a striking contrast between natural crystalline patterns and the case’s regular geometry.

Inside, the automatic Piaget 501P1 calibre delivers a 40-hour power reserve. It is a relaxed yet distinctive interpretation of the meteorite-dial concept.

Gérald Genta Gentissima Oursin 41

The Gérald Genta Gentissima Oursin has never shied away from unconventional design, and its meteorite-dial versions take that personality further.

Its 41mm titanium case is surrounded by 234 white-gold beads, creating the distinctive organic silhouette that gives the Oursin its name. A blue or green meteorite dial adds depth and natural irregularity.

Power comes from the automatic GG-005 calibre, operating at 4 Hz with a 50-hour power reserve. The result is a playful, technically considered watch that feels more like wearable design than a traditional instrument.

Frederique Constant Classic Power Reserve Big Date Manufacture Meteorite

Frederique Constant takes a more classical approach, pairing a meteorite dial with traditional complications.

The limited platinum edition features a blue Namibian meteorite dial in a 40mm case. Its display combines a big date, moonphase and power-reserve indication, powered by the manufacture FC-735 calibre.

Limited to 35 pieces, it demonstrates how meteorite can bring individuality to a traditional dress watch without compromising its classical character.

Furlan Marri Mechaquartz Chronograph Meteorite

Furlan Marri brings a distinctive take on meteorite with the Meteorite Octa, created to celebrate the brand’s fifth anniversary.

Its dial uses Muonionalusta iron meteorite, formed more than 4.5 billion years ago, in a striking sandwich construction that contrasts the raised meteorite centre with white subdials and an outer ring. Applied stainless-steel Roman numerals and a pulsometer scale complete the design.

Housed in a 38mm stainless-steel case measuring 12mm thick, the chronograph is powered by the Seiko V64 mechaquartz movement, combining quartz timekeeping with a mechanical chronograph module.

Kurono Tokyo Special Projects 37mm INSEKI

Kurono Tokyo brings its distinctive design language to meteorite with the Special Projects 37mm INSEKI, named after the Japanese word for meteorite.

Its 37mm stainless-steel case houses a Muonionalusta meteorite dial, framed by a white lacquered chapter ring and the brand’s Calligra typography. The contrast between the natural material and precise dial layout is central to its appeal.

The automatic Miyota 90S5 movement provides approximately 40 hours of power reserve. Each dial is personally inspected by Hajime Asaoka and receives his seal, reinforcing the watch’s emphasis on individuality.

A Piece of the Cosmos, Six Different Ways

Meteorite dials bring genuine individuality to watchmaking. Their naturally occurring patterns are impossible to replicate, while their extraterrestrial origins add a story beyond conventional materials and finishes.

These six watches showcase different interpretations of meteorite: Piaget complements an iconic design, Gérald Genta embraces a sculptural aesthetic, Frederique Constant takes a classical approach, while Furlan Marri and Kurono Tokyo explore more accessible, design-led expressions.

Armin Strom, however, takes the concept furthest mechanically. The Dual Time GMT Resonance Manufacture Edition Meteorite pairs an extraordinary fragment of space with a movement built around the fascinating phenomenon of resonance.

Here, the cosmos is not just on the dial; it is part of the conversation between two beating hearts.
